**TL;DR**

- **The driver changed on Friday, and it is no longer just AI credit.** **Brent broke $110** (close $109.86, +3.7%) and **WTI crossed $100** for the first time since September —
- Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure, Russia/Ukraine attacks on refineries, Hormuz shipping attacks. That is an **inflation shock**, which re-raises Fed-hike odds (the Fed already hiked 25bp in September).
- Tech shed **>$1T** in value Friday. **S&P -1.09%, Nasdaq -2.15%, SOX -3.83%, IGV -4.80%, ARKK -4.71%, VIX +21.45%.**
- **The long side is a single trade: energy.** Of the 55 names up ≥3%, the overwhelming majority are crude-levered —
- CRGY +10.07%, MTDR, AR, OVV, EQNR, EOG, VET, RRC, TALO, MUR, NOG, SM. XLF +0.45% was the only green S&P sector.
- **This is an inflation / risk-off rotation, not a growth tape** — and the same shock that bid oil is what repriced AI multiples down.
- **Two prior calls resolved, and both resolved against the bull case.** **BSP round-tripped completely** —
- +41.2% on the Berkshire placement (Oct 14), now -15.60% on a guidance miss, ~27% down in 5 sessions and **below the pre-Berkshire level**; Berkshire's $33 is now a ceiling.
- **CRWV is on day 3** of the credit unwind (-11.91%, near a 52-week low, −25% in a month). The AI complex has not found a bid.

**Cross-sectional structure**

- **Breadth is 125:55 and the losers are bigger.** 54 names moved ≥8%. The index looks survivable only because energy and financials are absorbing the cap-weighted damage.
- Nasdaq-100 was −2.5% and sits ~7% off the all-time high set *last week*.
- **Oil is the whole long side, and it is a geopolitical position.** Brent +3.7% to $109.86 on Houthi/Saudi escalation and Russia-Ukraine refinery strikes —
- **despite Hormuz volumes actually normalising** (>100M bbl last week; 40+ vessels in 24h). **The bid is risk premium, not physical scarcity.** Goldman puts the conflict premium at ~$24/bbl.
- That unwinds fast on a ceasefire headline.
- **The AI complex is de-rating for two stacked reasons that reinforce each other:** (1) **financing** — CRWV bond yields, Gartner's "most neoclouds won't survive standalone"; (2) **discount rate** —
- $110 oil re-raises hike odds. Optics, neocloud, bitcoin miners and software are all −10% to −12% with no single-name news.
- **Genuine idiosyncratic prints are rare, and mostly reversals.** BSP, GRAL and TLK are the only names on this board with a real company- or country-specific story.
- VICR and NBIS are pure beta.

**Needs human eyes warning**

- **BSP's $33 is now a ceiling, not support.** Berkshire bought 10M shares at $33 on Oct 14;
- the stock closed Friday at $47 after a guidance miss, ~27% down over five sessions and below its pre-placement level.
- The last brief called the 13% discount a bearish tell — that has played out.
- The IPO ($29, July) and the placement ($33) now bracket the float between two institutional anchors, with neither acting as support.
- **TLK is forced-selling flow, not a valuation call — and the clock is long.** MSCI's consultation runs to **Apr 30, 2027**; final decision by **Jun 30, 2027**.
- UBS estimates ~$4B passive + ~$15B active outflows. Telkom was the single largest net foreign sell on IDX.
- With the flow that large and the timeline that long, there is no natural bid until the consultation resolves. YTD already −47.6%.
- **Two earnings dates land inside the next week.** **VICR reports Q3 before the open on Oct 20** (consensus ~$187M revenue, +69% y/y; EPS $1.24–1.39;
- PT ~$392 against a $191 price) after five straight down days. **NBIS reports Oct 22.** VICR is the cleaner setup — the business is accelerating while the multiple compresses.
- NBIS is riskier: P/S 34 vs median 7, unprofitable, $8.55B of funding against a 600MW build.
- **The oil position is the crowded one, and it is a headline trade.** Brent's ~$24/bbl conflict premium is most of the move, and Hormuz volumes are actually *recovering*.
- The US offered up to 17M barrels of SPR on the same day and a House bill would block the Russia diesel deal.
- **Any ceasefire or de-escalation headline hits the entire long side of this brief simultaneously.**
- **GRAL is the one to actually check before the open.** −13% with XLV flat, after an ~85% one-month run, with the CEO selling 5.5% of his stake at $136.85 the day before.
- Consensus PT $119.80 sits almost exactly on the $117.81 close. NHS-Galleri and PATHFINDER 2 read out at ESMO — a binary event on a stock priced for the good outcome.
